subject: Science
title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
objectives: Children will sort leaves by size and shape with support.
Children will name fruits and say they come from plants.
content: Leaves of different shapes and sizes, flowers and their colours, and fruits that grow on plants.
teachingActivities: Use real leaves, flowers and fruits from the area; let children touch and sort; name colours and shapes; ask "Where does this fruit come from?"; check allergies before any tasting.
learnerActivities: Sort leaves by size and shape, name flower colours and name fruits that come from plants.
resources: Leaves of different sizes and shapes
assessment: Observe whether each child sorts leaves into big and small and names two fruits that grow on trees.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts leaves into big and small.
Names two fruits that grow on trees.

lessons.title: Big and small leaves
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort leaves into big and small.
successCriteria: Sorts leaves into big and small
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have planted seeds and know that plants need water, soil and sun.
resources: Two baskets labelled big and small
lessons.starter: Hold up a big leaf and a small leaf and say "This is big. This is small."
teacherActivities: Pass the leaves round and ask "Is it big or small?"
Put one leaf in each basket to show.
Let each child pick a leaf and choose a basket.
Look at the shapes of the leaves and talk about round and long.
learnerActivities: Children touch and say big or small.
Children watch and say the word.
Child sorts the leaf.
Child says round or long.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pass the leaves round and ask "Is it big or small?" Children: Children touch and say big or small.
Step 2. Teacher: Put one leaf in each basket to show. Children: Children watch and say the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a leaf and choose a basket. Children: Child sorts the leaf.
Step 4. Teacher: Look at the shapes of the leaves and talk about round and long. Children: Child says round or long.

practical.title: Leaf sort
steps: Put it in the big or small basket.
practical.safety: Use leaves from safe plants and wash hands afterwards. Do not allow leaves in mouths.

differentiation.support: Compare two leaves together and say big or small.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a leaf that is long and thin.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is this leaf big or small?

lessons.conclusion: Put the leaves back and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Collect two safe leaves and compare their size.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort leaves into big and small" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Flower colours
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name the colours of flowers.
successCriteria: Names at least three flower colours
Matches a flower to a colour card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have planted seeds and know that plants need water, soil and sun.
resources: Fresh flowers or large flower pictures in red, yellow, pink and white
lessons.starter: Show a red hibiscus and say "This flower is red. What colour is it?"
teacherActivities: Show each flower and name its colour.
Say "Find the yellow flower" and wait.
Match the flowers to the colour cards.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the colour.
Child points to the yellow flower.
Child places a flower on a colour card.
Child smells a flower and says nice.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each flower and name its colour. Children: Children look and say the colour.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Find the yellow flower" and wait. Children: Child points to the yellow flower.
Step 3. Teacher: Match the flowers to the colour cards. Children: Child places a flower on a colour card.
Step 4. Teacher: Smell the flowers gently. Children: Child smells a flower and says nice.

practical.title: Flower colours
steps: Match each to a colour card.
practical.safety: Check for allergies and pollen sensitivity first. Do not allow children to eat petals and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Offer two flowers and say the colour first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a flower with two colours.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the flowers in a vase and say "Thank you, flowers."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at flowers outside with your child and say their colours.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name the colours of flowers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Fruits from trees
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name fruits and say they grow on trees and plants.
successCriteria: Says that fruits grow on plants
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have planted seeds and know that plants need water, soil and sun.
resources: A mango, an orange, a banana and a pawpaw
lessons.starter: Hold up a mango and say "A mango grows on a mango tree. It comes from a plant."
teacherActivities: Show each fruit and its tree picture.
Ask "Where does the mango come from?"
Cut a fruit safely in half to show the seed inside.
Let each child pick a fruit and match it to its tree.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Child points to the tree picture.
Children look at the seed.
Child matches the fruit to a tree.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each fruit and its tree picture. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where does the mango come from?" Children: Child points to the tree picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Cut a fruit safely in half to show the seed inside. Children: Children look at the seed.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a fruit and match it to its tree. Children: Child matches the fruit to a tree.

practical.title: Fruit and tree
steps: Put fruit and tree pictures on the mat.
practical.safety: An adult cuts all fruit; check allergies first. Wash fruit and hands. Do not let children taste unless allergies are cleared.

differentiation.support: Offer two fruits and show the tree first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find the seed inside a fruit.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names fruits that grow on plants
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "Thank you, trees."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about where fruits come from when you eat them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name fruits and say they grow on trees and plants" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Fruit salad
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will make a fruit salad and say what each fruit is.
successCriteria: Names the fruits in the salad
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have planted seeds and know that plants need water, soil and sun.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we make a fruit salad." Show the fruits and ask "Which fruit is this?"
teacherActivities: Wash hands together and say why.
Show how to put pieces of fruit into the bowl.
Share the fruit salad in small cups.
learnerActivities: Children wash hands with soap.
Children add fruit pieces to the bowl.
Child stirs and says the names.
Child says thank you and tastes.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Wash hands together and say why. Children: Children wash hands with soap.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to put pieces of fruit into the bowl. Children: Children add fruit pieces to the bowl.
Step 3. Teacher: Stir the fruit together gently. Children: Child stirs and says the names.
Step 4. Teacher: Share the fruit salad in small cups. Children: Child says thank you and tastes.

practical.title: Fruit salad
steps: Add fruit pieces to a bowl.
practical.safety: An adult cuts fruit into very small pieces. Check allergies first and supervise closely for choking. Use clean spoons and bowls.

differentiation.support: Hold the bowl together and add the fruit.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name each fruit in the salad.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is in the fruit salad?

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "Thank you for the fruit."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a simple fruit salad at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a fruit salad and say what each fruit is" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 plants check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child sorts leaves and names fruits and flowers.
successCriteria: Names two fruits that grow on trees
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have planted seeds and know that plants need water, soil and sun.
lessons.starter: Sing the plant song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: leaves, flowers and fruits.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "What colour or size?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children wash hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: leaves, flowers and fruits. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "What colour or size?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Plant stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe plants and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two items.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend the fruit names.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts leaves by size; names flower colours; names fruits that grow on trees.

questions.question: Is this leaf big or small?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about leaves, flowers and fruits on walks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child sorts leaves and names fruits and flowers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
